scope: Bounded pinned Linux SPI-HID transport/current Darwin adapter and HID-event-path review, using existing saved non-sensitive numeric metadata and driver-name log lines. No source edits, builds, new acquisition, SSH, target access or human wait. This report is the only trackpad-task write.
verdict: Device 2 shares the already selected J293 SPI transport, but current PDM1SPIHID is deliberately keyboard-only. Adding a second descriptor alone is insufficient: a separate logical HID child and routing are missing; actual Linux binds device 2 to magicmouse; a vendor-mode/report decoder may be necessary; and generic touchpad contact events have no automatic PDHID mouse conversion for current Chonkstep. The exact device-2 descriptor, sizes and mode payload are not available in the reviewed evidence, so no decoder or descriptor can be specified honestly yet.

established_evidence.finding: Actual Linux log identifies magicmouse 001C:05AC:0341.0002 and Apple SPI Trackpad on 23510c000 SPI, plus hid-apple-mtp-haptic on .0003 / Apple SPI Actuator. Device-2 vendor decoding/haptics are not supplied by the SPI transport core itself. No private serial or input payload is copied here.

Independently hashed and inspected numeric driver lines: count 5, shared identity 05ac:0341 version 0175; only interface 1 country 33 / input 10 / output 2 / control 4086; keyboard descriptor length 90. No first device-1 input report observed. These are NOT device-2 metadata or its descriptor.

Logical management 0, keyboard 1, trackpad 2, actuator 3; per-interface HID object, descriptor, country and report limits; descriptor cap 512. Linux clamps enumeration to 4 even when actual shared count is 5; the fifth role is not established here.
All children inherit BUS_SPI and shared vendor/product/version; keyboard uses HID_TYPE_SPI_KEYBOARD, trackpad HID_TYPE_SPI_MOUSE, then hid_add_device selects the higher HID driver.

current_missing_adapter_work.gap: One metadata/descriptor store and one IOHIDDevice. Enumeration requests only interface 1 and its descriptor. poll sends only m1kbd_keyboard_input to this->handleReport; device 2/3 messages are consumed as otherMessages. The product string always identifies a keyboard.

Interface validator hard-requires 1; one-use semantic key mask contains only management plus iface1/desc1; input predicate only accepts outer device 1. The wire parser itself already admits devices 0..3 and d0; broadening device_ok is unnecessary.
The native class has no getReport/setReport overrides. IOHIDDevice defaults return Unsupported (IOHIDDevice.cpp:1739-1760), so any trackpad feature-mode operation cannot currently work through IOHID.

smallest_future_enumeration_scope.new_candidate_only: Keep rev005 and its packet frozen. Use a separate reviewed candidate and explicit opt-in for trackpad enumeration; do not silently enable feature writes or haptics.
smallest_future_enumeration_scope.reference: sources/linux-aurora-keyboard-reference/drivers/hid/spi-hid/spi-hid-apple-core.c:1120-1142 (executable calls; the older comment table repeats 0x10 for interface info and must not override these calls)
smallest_future_enumeration_scope.pairing: Extend the explicit one-use key set to exactly five enumeration keys: existing three plus iface2 and desc2. Preserve single outstanding request, 1-second deadline, CRC, flags/device/command/report/subdevice matching, no ID-echo check, and no retry. Claim before any ID increment/encode/write. Management is still requested once, not per child.
smallest_future_enumeration_scope.metadata: Validate a fixed 16-byte interface header with expected interface=2; keep its independent country/max-input/max-output/max-control. Preserve shared 05ac:0341 checks. Do not copy iface1 limits or validate unused optional string spans as essential identity. Unknown/incompatible lengths remain a real unsupported result.
smallest_future_enumeration_scope.bounds: Own a second descriptor copy of 1..512 real CRC-checked bytes. Current reassembly bounds a whole message to 2048 bytes, so effective input payload cap is 2038, not a guessed trackpad size. If actual metadata requires more, record/refuse and review rather than raising bounds silently.
smallest_future_enumeration_scope.observations: Numeric header/error diagnostics and descriptor length/hash/usage summary are sufficient for a first gap check. Do not log contact positions, key data, optional strings or serials. Store any necessary raw descriptor privately with exact provenance, not an invented replacement.

child_and_lifetime_design: Retain exactly one hardware owner, once-per-boot claim, PMGR/GPIO reset sequence, polling reader, workloop and protocol assembly state. A second independently matched PDM1SPIHID instance would be refused by the latch and must not independently reset or own this shared controller.

Smallest evolution can retain the keyboard IOHIDDevice as transport owner and attach one additional IOHIDDevice child for logical interface 2; a later parent-with-two-children refactor is optional, not necessary for initial enumeration. The child must have its own real descriptor and report limits, distinct stable interface identity/name, and the real shared vendor/product. Let IOHIDDevice construct its IOHIDInterface nubs from that descriptor; do not fake usage properties or concatenate colliding report-ID spaces.

Copy borrowed dlsp_message payload/descriptor before the next receive. Route flags=0x20, command=0x10 by outer device to the correct published child; feed complete descriptor-compatible payload bytes to that child only. Never infer that wire report number equals interface ID or prepend a guessed report ID.

Retain transport/child objects across callbacks. Quiesce routing and cancel/join polling before detaching children or releasing hardware maps. Trackpad initialization failure must be visibly failed/unsupported, not a successful empty child; do not repeat the shared hardware initialization. Preserve unload/termination refusal unless a separate actual quiescence design is established.

If feature I/O is later implemented, serialize it through the same gate and receive owner. Never wait for a timer callback blocked behind the gate currently held. A bounded synchronous response pump must preserve/routinely service other already-published child input or explicitly account for discarded input. Do not retain borrowed payload pointers or run a second serial/MMIO reader.

The engine has one partial-message assembly with complete-message interleaving support; concurrent fragmented streams are not proven. Add two-device routing/interleaving refusal tests before claiming support rather than assuming arbitrary fragment multiplexing.

vendor_decoder_assessment.confirmed: Saved Linux binds this device to magicmouse, not merely hid-generic. The pinned SPI source passes the raw payload directly to hid_input_report (lines 508-526) and parses the device-supplied descriptor (385-389); it contains no contact-coordinate decoder.
vendor_decoder_assessment.mode_hook_source: sources/linux-aurora-keyboard-reference/drivers/hid/spi-hid/spi-hid-apple-core.c:267 documents outer dev2 command0x52 report0x02 subdevice0x00 for multitouch mode. Lines392-432 implement generic feature GET (0x32) and SET (0x52), while438-452 implement OUTPUT (0x51). This establishes transport verbs, not the exact safe J293 mode payload or when to send it.
vendor_decoder_assessment.missing_primary_source: The acquired six-file reference set does not include drivers/hid/hid-magicmouse.c, the selected hid-apple-mtp-haptic implementation, or their matching/type tables. No local copies found. Their exact-pin source is needed in a separately authorized acquisition to derive payloads, packed touch layouts, capabilities and any mandatory enable/setup sequence.
vendor_decoder_assessment.darwin_generic_limit: IOHIDEventDriver parses standardized HID elements. Its Apple vendor-message handler wraps opaque data in vendorDefinedEvent, not decoded pointer contacts (parseVendorMessageElement:2442-2487, handleVendorMessageReport:4128-4197). Merely changing a personality or child name cannot decode packed Apple touch records.
vendor_decoder_assessment.honest_branch: If the actual device-2 descriptor and mode prove a normal mouse report is emitted, use that genuine standard path first. If touch contacts are vendor-packed, implement a bounded model-specific decoder/control path from exact source and real descriptor evidence. Until those are available, vendor decoder necessity for full multitouch is strongly indicated, while the exact available fallback mouse mode remains unknown.
vendor_decoder_assessment.haptic_boundary: Device3 is a separate actuator. Do not infer physical click behavior from successful device2 enumeration, nor write actuator commands without their own bounded source qualification. A pointer-only first path may defer haptics if source evidence shows they are not needed to obtain reports; that is presently unresolved.
vendor_decoder_assessment.unsafe_reference_copy: Do not copy Linux raw GET_REPORT memcpy at line422 using max(len,reply_len): it can exceed a caller buffer. Future adapter must reject oversize or use a properly bounded copy, with owned response storage and actual completion/error semantics.

darwin_to_desktop_gaps.finding: The actual combined IOHIDFamily personality does contain HID Pointer Driver for GenericDesktop Mouse/Pointer and Digitizer page 13. Do not mistake the narrower upstream Info-IOHIDEventDriver.plist for the built combined personality. A standard descriptor can match; a vendor-only top-level collection is not thereby a supported pointer.

TouchPad conformance enables digitizer collection dispatch. The driver emits a contact collection through dispatchEvent. That is not the same as dispatchRelativePointerEvent/dispatchAbsolutePointerEvent.

The PDHID queue bridge exists in relative/absolute pointer dispatch. Generic dispatchEvent routes to registered event clients and contains no digitizer-contact-to-PDHID mouse conversion. Therefore even valid generic touch contacts need an explicit pointer-policy consumer/bridge for current Chonkstep.
Keyboard and mouse nodes are lazy on first genuine queued events. No empty or fake queue publication is evidence of native input.
Current frozen NativeHid opens both keyboard and mouse character nodes; it consumes pointer records, not contact arrays.

Current seat supports keyboard and pointer with relative motion or normalized absolute position. There is no raw touch/contact/gesture pipeline. Event decoder and contact-to-relative-motion/lift/button policy must be explicit; mapping a trackpad contact directly to screen position is a different behavior, not a transparent equivalent.

missing_evidence: Actual device2 interface header (country and maximum report sizes), complete report descriptor bytes/hash and parsed usages/report IDs.
Exact pinned magicmouse matcher/decoder and any device2 feature-mode requests/payloads. The Linux runtime driver name alone does not reveal bytes or coordinate layouts.
Whether default firmware supplies a usable standard relative-pointer fallback without mode changes; no report or descriptor in this review proves that.
Any necessary relation between device2 input and device3 actuator initialization, including physical button sensing without haptic setup.
Native Darwin input reports, event-driver matching/decoding, queue publication and actual physical pointer/button behavior. Existing keyboard enumeration proves none of these.
Sustained two-device service fairness and multi-packet behavior under real simultaneous activity; existing keyboard-only host tests are not that proof.
ordered_next_steps: Preserve rev005. Obtain the missing exact-pin vendor decoder/matcher source in a separately authorized source acquisition, and inspect any already captured descriptor before proposing feature writes. No fetch performed here.

Prepare a separate bounded interface2 metadata/descriptor-only candidate with explicit one-use keys, separate storage and no mode/haptic writes. Add fake tests for wrong subdevice, duplicates, non-echo response IDs, oversize metadata/descriptors, CRC and truncation.

Review a single-owner/two-child routing and lifecycle implementation with fake callbacks: keyboard unchanged, trackpad data never sent to keyboard, no delivery before child ready, teardown blocks callbacks and unmaps last, request timeouts cannot deadlock the polling owner. Preserve protocol bounds.

Choose the actual report route from descriptor/source evidence: genuine standard mouse if present, otherwise a bounded vendor decoder plus explicit contact-to-pointer policy. Test report-ID/length/contact-count/sign/bounds, lift/reset/button release, and malformed input producing no events; leave unsupported modes/errors explicit.

Only a later separately authorized physical test can establish native input. Registry presence or host-origin virtual HID is not that evidence. No hardware/human action requested or waited for in this review.
